review.summary: JuliaSyntax accepted `"$(x, digits=1)"` as a valid interpolation of a tuple, while the Julia reference parser (fl_parse) rejects it with 'invalid interpolation syntax'. The fix checks, after parse_atom, whether the parsed construct is actually a `parens` node; if not (e.g. a `tuple-p`), it emits an error node. This is a genuine divergence from documented/reference parser behavior, not a new feature.
review.evidence: Issue #305 shows a concrete reproducible divergence: parsestmt(Expr, "\"$(x, digits=1)\"") returns :("$((x, digits = 1))") whereas fl_parse raises ParseError("invalid interpolation syntax"). PR #306 states the fix and 'Fixes #305', matching the commit content. Minimized patch is a single hunk in src/parser.jl parse_string, adding a position marker and an emit(..., K"error") when peek_behind(skip_parens=false).kind != K"parens"; the other two hunks are a docstring update and a peek->peek_token refactor, and minimization reports the single hunk as globally minimal and sufficient. Tests were updated in test/parser.jl, and the inline comment documents the expected parse: "$(x,y)" ==> (string (error (tuple-p x y))). Runtime evidence reports a stable_differential across 3 repetitions with the full suite passing on the fixed version.
review.missing_evidence: No explicit trigger test names are listed, and the test diff itself is not shown, so the exact failing assertion on the parent commit is not directly visible. PR number/body metadata is empty in the record aside from the linked issue records.
review.validation_risks: The change makes the parser stricter, so previously-passing reference tests or downstream expectations that relied on tuple interpolation parsing could shift; verify no other suite cases regress. Because the fix surfaces as an error node rather than a value change, a reviewer could argue it is diagnostics-only; here the parse tree itself changes (error wrapping tuple-p), so it is a behavioral fix in a parser. Also confirm the non-minimized peek_token refactor hunk is not required for the trigger test to fail/pass as expected.
review.suggested_tests: Assert parsestmt/parse of "\"$(x, digits=1)\"" and "\"$(x,y)\"" produce (string (error (tuple-p ...))) and that Expr conversion raises ParseError with 'invalid interpolation syntax'; add the semicolon variant "\"$(x; y)\""; add negative controls that must remain valid: "\"a $(x + y) b\"" ==> (string "a " (parens (call-i x + y)) " b"), "\"hi$(\"ho\")\"", "\"$x\"", and "\"$(f(x, y))\"" (commas inside a nested call must stay legal); cross-check each against fl_parse for reference-parser agreement.

swe.problem_statement:
Disallow tuples as atoms in interpolation syntax
There's an error reporting inconsistency with the reference parser for commas in brackets in interpolations:

```julia
julia> JuliaSyntax.parsestmt(Expr, "\"\$(x, digits=1)\"")
:("$((x, digits = 1))")

julia> JuliaSyntax.fl_parse(Expr, "\"\$(x, digits=1)\"")
ERROR: ParseError("invalid interpolation syntax")
Stacktrace:
 [1] fl_parse(str::String, pos::Int64; greedy::Bool, raise::Bool, depwarn::Bool)
   @ JuliaSyntax ~/.julia/dev/JuliaSyntax/src/hooks.jl:379 [inlined]
```

Found in https://github.com/JuliaLang/julia/issues/18703#issuecomment-1583988716
swe.patch:
diff --git a/src/parse_stream.jl b/src/parse_stream.jl
index d21260ba..f37a1f59 100644
--- a/src/parse_stream.jl
+++ b/src/parse_stream.jl
@@ -534,7 +534,7 @@ function peek_full_token(stream::ParseStream, n::Integer=1;
 end
 
 """
-    peek_behind(ps; skip_trivia=true)
+    peek_behind(ps; skip_trivia=true, skip_parens=true)
     peek_behind(ps, pos::ParseStreamPosition)
 
 Return information about a span which was previously inserted into the output,
diff --git a/src/parser.jl b/src/parser.jl
index 72fbd1d3..385c0da2 100644
--- a/src/parser.jl
+++ b/src/parser.jl
@@ -2097,7 +2097,8 @@ function parse_function_signature(ps::ParseState, is_function::Bool)
             is_empty_tuple = peek(ps, skip_newlines=true) == K")"
             opts = parse_brackets(ps, K")") do _, _, _, _
                 _parsed_call = was_eventually_call(ps)
-                _is_anon_func = peek(ps, 2) ∉ KSet"( ." && !_parsed_call
+                t2 = peek_token(ps, 2)
+                _is_anon_func = kind(t2) ∉ KSet"( ." && !_parsed_call
                 return (needs_parameters = _is_anon_func,
                         is_anon_func     = _is_anon_func,
                         parsed_call      = _parsed_call)
@@ -3178,7 +3179,12 @@ function parse_string(ps::ParseState, raw::Bool)
             if k == K"("
                 # "a $(x + y) b"  ==>  (string "a " (parens (call-i x + y)) " b")
                 # "hi$("ho")"     ==>  (string "hi" (parens (string "ho")))
+                m = position(ps)
                 parse_atom(ps)
+                if peek_behind(ps, skip_parens=false).kind != K"parens"
+                    # "$(x,y)" ==> (string (error (tuple-p x y)))
+                    emit(ps, m, K"error", error="invalid interpolation syntax")
+                end
             elseif k == K"var"
                 # var identifiers disabled in strings
                 # "$var"  ==>  (string var)
swe.test_patch:
diff --git a/test/parser.jl b/test/parser.jl
index b6a8d836..a1e71ce4 100644
--- a/test/parser.jl
+++ b/test/parser.jl
@@ -869,6 +869,8 @@ tests = [
         "\"\"\"\n\$x\n a\"\"\"" => "(string-s x \"\\n\" \" a\")"
         "\"a \$(x + y) b\""  =>  "(string \"a \" (parens (call-i x + y)) \" b\")"
         "\"hi\$(\"ho\")\""   =>  "(string \"hi\" (parens (string \"ho\")))"
+        "\"\$(x,y)\""        =>  "(string (error (tuple-p x y)))"
+        "\"\$(x;y)\""        =>  "(string (error (block-p x y)))"
         "\"a \$foo b\""  =>  "(string \"a \" foo \" b\")"
         "\"\$var\""      =>  "(string var)"
         "\"\$outer\""    =>  "(string outer)"
FAIL_TO_PASS: Parser does not crash on broken code
swe.pr_description:
Commas and semicolons are not allowed within string interpolation brackets. For example `"$(x, digits=2)"` is reserved syntax.

Fixes #305

llm_metadata.reasoning: The issue requests that interpolations like "$(x,y)" be treated as invalid syntax, matching the reference parser's error, and provides example behavior and an external comment link. The added tests assert that such interpolations produce an error node (tuple-p and block-p), which directly reflects the described intent, showing clear alignment. No signs of test‑suite coupling, implicit naming, external dependency reliance, ambiguity, extraneous patch artifacts, or hidden domain knowledge are present. Therefore the task is well‑specified and solvable (code A).

mwe_basis.defect: JuliaSyntax accepted comma/semicolon tuple-like forms inside string interpolation instead of reporting invalid interpolation syntax
